shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading away my only A for a second B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C - reducing variety since I'd have none of one good. Current even distribution (1 each) is already balanced; this trade doesn't improve variety-based utility.
Trading 1B for 1A would just swap my current equal distribution (1,1,1) into (2A,1C,0B), reducing variety instead of improving it. Since I value variety, this would lower my utility.
Giving up my only B to get more A would leave me with none of B, hurting variety; current balanced holdings (1 each) are more valuable to me than an unbalanced bundle with 3 A and 0 B.
Trading away C would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility since I'd go from (1,1,1) to (0,1,2), which is less balanced than my current equal distribution.
This trade would give me 2C and 0B, reducing variety (currently 1-1-1 balanced). Since I value variety, going to 2-1-0 decreases utility rather than improving it.
Giving up my only B to get more C would leave me with zero B, hurting variety even though I'd gain extra C. Not worth it.
Trading 1A for 1B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety (1,1,1 to 0,2,1), which decreases my utility since I value balanced holdings.
Trading away my only B to get a second A would unbalance my holdings (2A,0B,1C) rather than improve variety. I prefer to keep an even spread, so this trade doesn't increase my utility.
This trade would leave me with 0 B and 3 A, creating an imbalanced inventory. I value variety, so I'd rather keep some B and gain A more moderately.

Trading away my only C to get a second B would leave me with 0 C, 1 A, 2 B - reducing variety and giving me a surplus in B while eliminating C entirely. Since I value variety, this worsens my utility rather than improving it.
Current inventory is balanced at 1 each. Trading away B to get more C would create imbalance (2C,1A,0B), reducing variety value. Not beneficial.
Giving up my only B to get more C would leave me with zero B, hurting variety balance more than the extra C is worth.
I currently have 0 C, 2 A, 0 B. Trading 1 A for 1 B gives me 1 A and 1 B, increasing variety across my bundle (A2,B0 -> A1,B1), which raises utility under my variety-preferring preferences.
Giving up both my A for only 1 B would leave me with just one good type again, not improving variety. I'd rather trade only 1 A for 1 B to diversify while keeping some A.

This trade would give me 2×B and 0×A, moving away from variety rather than toward it. Since I currently have equal amounts of C, A, and B (1 each), trading away my only A for a second B reduces diversity and lowers my utility.
Current inventory is balanced (1 each). Trading away B for A would just shift imbalance to B=0, A=2, not improving variety-based utility. No net gain.
Giving up my only B to end up with 0 B and 3 A hurts variety; I'd rather keep some B and get a smaller A increase.
I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of C, A, and B. Trading away my only C for an extra B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility rather than improving it.

This trade would give me 2C and 0B, reducing variety (2,1,0) instead of keeping balanced (1,1,1). Since I value variety, trading away my only B for a second C decreases utility rather than improving it.
Giving up my only B would leave me with zero of that good, hurting variety, while I'd have 3 C which is already diminishing in value. Not a good trade for my variety-seeking preferences.

Currently I have C:1, A:1, B:0. Trading 1A for 1B gives me C:1, A:0, B:1 - this maintains variety across 2 goods but doesn't increase my count of distinct goods held. However, giving up A (which I have 1 of) for B (which I have 0 of) increases variety value since B was previously unrepresented - net improvement given diminishing value of goods I already hold.

Trading my only C for B gives me a balanced 0C,1A,1B->1A,1B,0C inventory; since I value variety, going from (1,1,0) to (0,1,1) keeps equal diversity but acquiring B (currently zero) increases marginal value more than losing a C which I'd then have zero of too - net it's a lateral move but balances toward having one of each eventually. Actually this results in zero C, which reduces variety. Reconsider: current (C1,A1,B0); after trade (C0,A1,B1) - still only 2 types held, same variety count, so neutral trade, but B's marginal value was higher than C's since B=0. Accept as it improves utility slightly.
Trading away my only A for a second B would reduce variety - I'd go from (1,1,1) to (1,0,2), which is less balanced and lowers utility given my preference for variety.
This trade would give me 2A and 0B, reducing variety (1C,1A,1B -> 1C,2A,0B), which decreases my utility since I value balanced holdings. I'd rather keep my even distribution.
Giving up my only B to get more A reduces variety, lowering overall utility since I'd have zero B while A becomes overrepresented.

I currently have equal amounts of C, A, and B (1 each). Trading away my only C for another B would make my inventory 0 C, 1 A, 2 B, reducing variety and lowering utility since I'd go from 1 of each to lacking C entirely while doubling up on B.
Trading away my only B to get a second C would reduce variety (C:2,A:1,B:0), which is worse than my current balanced C:1,A:1,B:1 bundle under a variety-preferring utility function.
Trading away my only B to get more C would leave me with zero variety in B and an unbalanced bundle (3,1,0), which is worse under my variety-preferring utility than keeping an even (1,1,1) split.

Trading A (which I have 1 of) for B (which I have 0 of) improves variety across C, A, B, moving from (1,1,0) to (1,0,1) - equally diverse but fills a missing good category, matching my preference for variety.

Current inventory C:1,A:1,B:0. Trading away 1 C (dropping to 0) for 1 B (going to 1) gives me a more even spread across A, B, with 0 C - but better: result would be C:0,A:1,B:1. Actually this gives variety across A and B, avoiding having 2 of one and 0 of another... but I'd have 0 C. Still, since I value variety and currently have zero B, gaining B while losing one of two C-equivalent units improves balance, moving from (1,1,0) to (0,1,1), which maintains equal spread across two goods and introduces a new good I lack entirely - net utility gain from diversification outweighs the loss of a single C unit.
Trading 1A for 1B would leave me with 2B and 0A, reducing variety (1,0,2) which is worse than my current balanced (1,1,1) inventory. I prefer to keep diversity across all three goods.

Trading 1B for 1A would just swap my balanced 1-1-1 inventory into 2A/0B, reducing variety instead of improving it. Since I value variety and currently hold equal amounts, this trade decreases my utility.
Giving up my only B to end up with 0 B and 3 A reduces variety, which I value. Not a good trade for my preferences.
Trading my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C, 1 A, 2 B, reducing variety and concentrating in B which I'd value less. I prefer to keep balanced holdings across all three goods.
Trading 1 B for 1 C would leave me with 2C,1A,0B, reducing variety instead of improving it. Since I value equal distribution, this trade decreases my utility.
Giving up my only B would leave me with zero variety in that good while stacking up C, which hurts my preference for balanced holdings.

Current inventory C:1, A:1, B:0. Trading away A(1) for B(1) gives C:1,A:0,B:1 - still uneven but shifts variety deficit from B to A equally, same total diversity. Actually better: moving from (1,1,0) to (1,0,1) is symmetric in utility, but having B for the first time adds marginal value since B was most scarce (0). This improves variety balance since now I hold two distinct goods including the previously absent one, same as before essentially a lateral trade, but since B was strictly scarcer (0 vs 1), gaining it is favorable.

Currently I have 1C, 1A, 0B. Trading 1C for 1B gives me 0C,1A,1B - achieving perfect variety across having A and B instead of duplicate C, which matches my preference for variety since having zero of a good is worse than having one of each.
Current inventory is 1-1-1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only A for an extra B would make me 1-0-2, reducing variety and overall utility since I'd have zero of A.

Current inventory is balanced (1 each). Trading away B for A would just shift which good I have 0 of, not improve variety - I'd go from 1/1/1 to 2/0/1, which is worse since I'd have none of B instead of an even spread.
Giving up my only B to get 3 A would leave me with zero variety in B, which hurts my utility since I value diversity across goods.

Trading C for B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and making my bundle less balanced. I'd prefer to keep an even spread of 1 each or increase scarce goods rather than swap one scarce good for a duplicate.
This trade would give me C:2, A:1, B:0, reducing variety and concentrating goods in C while leaving me with none of B. Since I value variety, this would decrease my utility rather than improve it.
Trading away my only B would leave me with zero of that good, hurting variety. I value having at least one of each good more than accumulating extra C.
